mainTopic: Laundering a חטאת stain, which vessels need מריקה ושטיפה, and when fire can clean absorbed taste from ovens, pots and tiles
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining how urine is used when laundering a garment stained with חטאת blood. The urine is blended into tasteless saliva, which goes along with every one of the seven cleaning substances. A new משנה then teaches that a vessel needs מריקה ושטיפה whether holy meat was cooked in it or poured into it boiling. רבי שמעון exempts קדשים קלים. A ברייתא learns the 'poured in boiling' case from the full פסוק. רמי בר חמא asks whether cooking without absorption, such as meat hanging inside an earthenware oven, requires breaking the oven. Two proofs are offered and both are pushed off. Next, רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי's ruling that bread from a fat-smeared oven is forbidden forever is refuted by a ברייתא, which says firing up the oven is enough. This leads רבינא to ask why רב requires pots to be broken for פסח. The גמרא gives two answers: metal versus earthenware, or heat from inside versus heat from outside. It ends by ruling that a clay baking tile heated from outside stays forbidden.

steps.title: Mixing the urine in with all seven substances at once is rejected
steps.stepSummary: A suggestion that the urine is hidden by applying all seven substances together is rejected from a משנה that says doing them all at once accomplishes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the urine is mixed in with the seven substances and all of them are applied together as one, that cannot be. We learned in a משנה: if he applied them out of order, or applied all seven at once, he has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one way to use the urine so it is not noticeable by itself: blend it with all seven substances at once. It immediately knocks this down from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea was that if everything goes on together, the urine never shows up as a separate item. But the משנה in נדה says the seven substances must be used one after another, in order. Putting all seven on together is invalid, so this cannot be how it is done.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible suggestion)
It is absorbed / swallowed up (blended in)
The seven cleaning substances used to test and clean a stain
He did nothing at all, meaning the action is invalid

phrases.english: And if you would say that it is absorbed
phrases.notes: "It" here is the urine, one of the seven cleaning substances.

phrases.english: together with the seven substances,
and he applies all of them as one;
but didn't we learn:
if he applied them not in their order
or if he applied all seven of them at once –
he has done nothing at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּמַבְלַע לְהוּ בַּהֲדֵי שִׁבְעָה סַמְמָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (before this section) about how urine is used in laundering the stain.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that the urine is blended into all seven substances applied together.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה rules that applying all seven at once is invalid.

steps.title: Mixing the urine in with just one substance is also rejected
steps.stepSummary: A second suggestion, that the urine is blended with only one substance, is rejected because each substance needs three separate rubbings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the urine is mixed in with just one of the substances, that cannot be either. We learned that one must rub three times with each and every substance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a smaller version: hide the urine inside just one other substance. This is also rejected from the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the urine rode along with another substance, it would not get its own three rubbings. The משנה requires three rubbings for every single substance, so the urine cannot just be folded into a different one.

phrases.english: And if you would say that it is absorbed
together with one of the substances –
but one must rub three times
with each and every one, we learned!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּמַיבְלַע לְהוּ בַּהֲדֵי חַד מִסַּמְמָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 'all seven at once' idea fails, a narrower suggestion is tried and also rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects blending the urine with a single other substance.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Every substance needs its own three rubbings, so the urine cannot be hidden inside another one.

steps.title: The urine is blended into tasteless saliva
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the urine is mixed into tasteless saliva, which רישׁ לקישׁ says goes along with every substance anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the urine is absorbed in tasteless saliva. As רישׁ לקישׁ said: tasteless saliva must be used together with each and every substance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer: the urine is mixed into the tasteless saliva. It supports this with a statement of רישׁ לקישׁ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tasteless saliva is not just one step in the list. According to רישׁ לקישׁ it goes along with every one of the substances. So blending the urine into it does not break the order and does not take away anyone's three rubbings, and the urine is still not noticeable by itself.
steps.whatToRemember: The urine is used inside the tasteless saliva, because that saliva goes along with every substance. This avoids both problems from the משנה.

phrases.english: Rather, it is absorbed in tasteless saliva.
phrases.notes: Tasteless saliva is the spit of someone who has not eaten yet that day.

phrases.english: As Reish Lakish said:
Tasteless saliva must be
with each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer that survives both rejections.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines how the urine is used: inside the saliva, which accompanies every substance.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The urine is hidden within all seven substances together, or within one other substance.
steps.terutzMaskana: The urine is hidden within tasteless saliva, which is used with every substance (רישׁ לקישׁ).

steps.title: משנה: which vessels need scouring and rinsing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a vessel needs מריקה ושטיפה whether the קדשים were cooked in it or poured into it boiling, and for both levels of holiness. רבי שמעון exempts קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether a vessel had קדשים cooked in it or had boiling קדשים poured into it, and whether they were קדשי קדשים or קדשים קלים, the vessel needs scouring and rinsing. רבי שמעון says: for קדשים קלים, the vessel does not need scouring and rinsing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists which vessels need מריקה ושטיפה after holy meat was in them hot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה widens the rule in two ways. It covers a vessel that only had boiling meat poured into it, not just one used for cooking. It also covers both levels of holiness. רבי שמעון disagrees on the second point and limits the rule to קדשי קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the most holy level
Scouring and rinsing (of a metal vessel)

phrases.english: MISHNA: Whether one cooked in it
or one poured boiling into it,
whether offerings of the most sacred order
phrases.notes: Some versions say הקדשים, in round brackets; the corrected wording is קֳּדָשִׁים, in square brackets. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: or offerings of lesser sanctity –
they require scouring and rinsing.
Rabbi Shimon says: offerings of lesser sanctity
do not require scouring and rinsing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֶחָד שֶׁבִּישֵּׁל בּוֹ וְאֶחָד שֶׁעֵירָה לְתוֹכוֹ רוֹתֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה, unrelated to the laundering discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vessels need מריקה ושטיפה whether the meat was cooked in them or poured in boiling, for all קדשים. רבי שמעון exempts קדשים קלים.

steps.title: ברייתא: where do we learn the 'poured in boiling' case?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא notes that the פסוק speaks of cooking, and asks what source covers a vessel that only had boiling food poured into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'in which it is cooked' only teaches about a vessel used for cooking. From where do we know the same for a vessel that had boiling food poured into it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that looks for the source of the משנה's first point. It sets up the question; the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain words of the פסוק mention only cooking. So the ברייתא asks how we know that pouring boiling meat into a vessel counts the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (this case from the words)

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
"In which it is cooked" –
I have only a vessel in which one cooked;
if one poured boiling into it, from where?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֲשֶׁר תְּבֻשַּׁל בּוֹ אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁבִּישֵּׁל בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of the משנה's ruling about a vessel with boiling food poured into it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that a vessel with boiling food poured into it is treated like one used for cooking.

steps.title: The fuller verse covers the poured-in case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the fuller wording of the פסוק: 'and in which it is cooked shall be broken.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the vessel in which it is cooked shall be broken.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question by quoting more of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read in full, the פסוק puts the focus on the meat being hot inside the vessel ('in which it is'). So a vessel counts whether the meat was cooked in it or was poured into it boiling.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall be broken (said about an earthenware vessel)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'poured in boiling' case is learned from the full פסוק, 'and in which it is cooked shall be broken.'

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And that in which it is cooked shall be broken."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:21. The ברייתא reads the full phrase as covering any vessel the hot meat is in.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וַאֲשֶׁר תְּבֻשַּׁל בּוֹ יִשָּׁבֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fuller wording of the פסוק includes a vessel that had boiling meat poured into it.

steps.title: Meat roasted hanging inside an earthenware oven
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks whether meat of a חטאת roasted while hanging in the airspace of an earthenware oven makes the oven need breaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: if someone hung the meat in the air of an oven, what is the law? Is the Torah particular only about cooking together with absorption, or even about cooking without absorption?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא asks a new question about meat that is cooked by an oven but never touches its walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hanging meat gets cooked by the oven's heat, but no taste soaks into the walls. So the question is what the Torah's demand to break the vessel depends on: both cooking and absorption, or cooking alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked a question it was unsure about
The empty air space inside an oven
Absorption of taste into the vessel's walls
The Torah (literally, the Merciful One) is particular about

steps.whyThisMatters: This question frames the rest of the passage. Both proofs that follow are tested against it.

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama asked:
If he hung it in the airspace of an oven, what is the law?
phrases.notes: "It" is the meat of a חטאת, and the oven is an earthenware one.

phrases.english: Is it about cooking and absorption together
that the Merciful One is particular,
or perhaps even about cooking without absorption?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule that a vessel used for קדשים needs breaking, and asks what exactly triggers it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does cooking without absorption obligate breaking an earthenware vessel?

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about pouring
steps.stepSummary: רבא tries to prove the answer from the משנה, which puts cooking in a vessel and pouring boiling food into it on the same level.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear: "Whether one cooked in it or one poured boiling food into it."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings the משנה's words as a proof that one of the two things alone is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring boiling food into a vessel causes absorption without real cooking, yet the משנה still requires treatment. רבא wants to learn from this that cooking and absorption do not both have to happen.

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
Whether one cooked in it
or one poured boiling food into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a proof for the question in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That cooking and absorption do not both need to happen.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: whether one cooked in it or poured boiling food into it.

steps.title: That proof covers the wrong case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Pouring is absorption without cooking, which was never in doubt. The question is about cooking without absorption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Absorption without cooking was not our question. Our question is cooking without absorption: what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off רבא's proof by showing it proves the opposite case from the one being asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's pouring case has absorption, and absorption alone clearly matters, since the taste stays stuck in earthenware. The hanging-meat case has cooking with no absorption, and the משנה says nothing about that.

keyTerms.meaning: We did not have a question about this

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two cases apart. Pouring is absorption without cooking. Hanging meat is cooking without absorption. Only the second one is in doubt.

phrases.english: Absorption without cooking:
we did not ask about that.
When we asked,
it was about cooking without absorption. What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּלּוּעַ בְּלֹא בִּישּׁוּל לָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 8.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה deals with absorption without cooking, not cooking without absorption.

steps.title: Proof from the metal oven of the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a new proof. The oven in the מקדש was made of metal. If cooking without absorption did not matter, it could have been made of earthenware.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה that the oven of the מקדש was made of metal. If cooking without absorption did not matter, they should have made it of earthenware!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof, from the fact that the oven of the מקדש was metal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is that the oven was made of metal so it would not need breaking. If roasting hanging meat, with no absorption, did not require breaking, an earthenware oven would have worked. So cooking alone must matter.

keyTerms.meaning: The oven used in the בית המקדש
And if you would think, which sets up an argument

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav Naḥman said
that Rabba bar Avuh said:

phrases.aramaic: תַּנּוּר שֶׁל מִקְדָּשׁ – שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת הָיָה.
phrases.english: The oven of the Temple was made of metal.
And if it enters your mind
that about cooking without absorption the Torah is not particular,
then let them make it of earthenware!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof fails, a new proof is tried.
steps.raayaObject: That cooking without absorption does require breaking.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the oven of the מקדש was made of metal.

steps.title: The oven was metal because of baked meal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The oven had to be metal anyway, because the leftovers of the מנחות were baked in it with both cooking and absorption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since leftovers of meal offerings were baked in the oven, and that involves both cooking and absorption, we make it of metal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the second proof by giving a different reason why the oven was metal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Baked dough touches the oven walls, so there is both cooking and absorption, and an earthenware oven would need breaking for that reason alone. So the metal oven proves nothing about cooking without absorption. The question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover parts of meal offerings, eaten by the כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: Pouring shows that absorption alone matters. Whether cooking without absorption matters, as with meat hanging in an oven, is still unresolved here, because both proofs were pushed off.

phrases.english: Since there are the remainders of meal offerings
which are baked in the oven,
and there is both cooking and absorption,
we make it of metal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the metal oven completely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The oven had to be metal anyway because of baking, which involves both cooking and absorption.

steps.title: רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי forbids bread from a fat-smeared oven forever
steps.stepSummary: An oven was smeared with fat. רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי forbade eating bread baked in it forever, even with plain salt, in case someone eats it with כותח, a milk dip.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an oven that was smeared with fat. רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי forbade eating bread from it forever, even with salt, because someone might come to eat it with כותח, a milk dip.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a ruling. רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי says bread from an oven smeared with meat fat is forbidden forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bread picks up meat taste from the fat in the oven. Eating it with salt alone is not a problem, but he forbids even that so a person will not end up eating it with a milk food, which would be בשר בחלב. The word 'forever' shows he holds the fat can never be fully removed from the oven.

keyTerms.meaning: כותח, a dip made with milk

phrases.english: There was a certain oven that was smeared with fat,
Rabba bar Ahilai forbade
eating the bread from it forever,
and even eating it with salt,
lest one come to eat it with kutach.
phrases.notes: כותח is a dip made with milk, so eating this meat-flavored bread with it would be meat with milk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about absorbed taste in an oven. It is related to the earlier steps' theme of vessels that absorb, but it is a separate case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread baked in an oven smeared with fat is forbidden forever, even with salt, in case it is eaten with a milk dip.

steps.title: A ברייתא says firing the oven makes the bread permitted again
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that dough kneaded with milk is forbidden. In the same way, bread from an oven smeared with tail fat is forbidden, but only until the oven is fired up again.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him from a ברייתא: One may not knead dough with milk. If he did, all the bread is forbidden, because people may get used to sinning. In the same way, one may not smear an oven with tail fat. If he did, all the bread is forbidden until he fires up the oven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says the oven problem lasts only until the oven is fired up again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees that bread from a fat-smeared oven is forbidden, for the same reason as milky dough. But it adds a limit, 'until he fires up the oven.' That means firing the oven removes the fat, which goes against רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי's word 'forever.'

keyTerms.meaning: the fat tail of a sheep, which counts as meat
that he fires up (heats) the oven

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One may not knead dough with milk,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָשׁ – כׇּל הַפַּת כּוּלָּהּ אֲסוּרָה,
phrases.english: and if he kneaded it, all of the bread is forbidden,
because one might get used to sin.
phrases.notes: People normally eat bread with meat, so someone might eat this milky bread with meat without thinking.

phrases.aramaic: כְּיוֹצֵא בּוֹ – אֵין טָשִׁין אֶת הַתַּנּוּר בְּאַלְיָה,
phrases.english: Similarly, one may not smear an oven with tail fat,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם טָשׁ – כׇּל הַפַּת כּוּלָּהּ אֲסוּרָה,
phrases.english: and if he smeared it, all of the bread is forbidden,
until he fires up the oven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 12 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי's ruling that the bread is forbidden forever
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits the ban with 'until he fires up the oven,' so firing removes the fat and the ban is not forever.

steps.title: רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares the ברייתא a refutation of רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי and agrees that it is a real refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי! It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי's ruling is wrong. No answer is offered for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the גמרא says 'תיובתא' twice like this, it means the challenge stands and the opinion is rejected. So the ברייתא stands: firing up the oven is enough to permit the bread, though the גמרא soon limits which ovens this applies to.

keyTerms.meaning: a refutation; the opinion cannot stand

steps.whatToRemember: According to the ברייתא, an oven smeared with meat fat becomes usable again after it is fired up. רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי's 'forever' is rejected.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Rabba bar Ahilai!
It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 13 by accepting it as final.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ruling that the bread is forbidden forever is rejected; firing up the oven removes the fat.

steps.title: Why then must pots be broken for פסח?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי: if firing an oven removes what it absorbed, why does רב say pots must be broken for פסח?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Since רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי was refuted, why did רב say that pots must be broken for פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא raises a new difficulty that comes out of the conclusion. If firing cleans an oven, it seems pots with חמץ could also be cleaned by fire instead of being broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא showed that fire can burn out absorbed taste. רב's ruling that pots must be broken suggests absorbed taste can never come out. The two seem to clash.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּאִיתּוֹתַב רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי,
phrases.english: Now since Rabba bar Ahilai was refuted,
why did Rav say:
pots on Pesach must be broken?
phrases.notes: He means pots that were used for חמץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּאִיתּוֹתַב רַבָּה בַּר אֲהִילַיי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion of step 14 and uses it to challenge a ruling of רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that pots must be broken for פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If fire removes absorbed taste, as the ברייתא shows, the pots should be fixable by firing them, not by breaking them.

steps.title: The ברייתא is talking about a metal oven
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that רב reads the ברייתא as talking about a metal oven, which fire can clean. Pots made of earthenware are different.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רב explains that ברייתא as talking about an oven made of metal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא. The ברייתא about firing the oven is about a metal oven, so it does not tell us anything about earthenware pots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fire can burn absorbed taste out of metal. Earthenware is different: what it absorbs cannot be fully removed, so earthenware pots must be broken. This fits the earlier steps, where an earthenware vessel that absorbed must be broken.

keyTerms.meaning: sets it in a specific case; explains it as talking about

steps.whatToRemember: Firing cleans a metal vessel, but an earthenware vessel that absorbed cannot be cleaned and must be broken. So the ברייתא (metal oven) and רב (earthenware pots) do not clash.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא and רב disagree. They are talking about different materials: metal can be cleaned by fire, earthenware cannot.
steps.whyThisMatters: According to this answer, the material of a vessel decides whether fire can clean it, which matters for koshering vessels. Step 17 gives a second way to explain the difference.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַב מוֹקֵי לַהּ הָהִיא
phrases.english: He said to him: Rav sets that ruling
phrases.notes: 'That ruling' is the ברייתא about firing up the oven.

phrases.english: as talking about an oven made of metal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מוֹקֵי לַהּ הָהִיא בְּשֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by limiting the ברייתא to metal ovens.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is set in a metal oven.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since firing cleaned the oven in the ברייתא, firing should also clean earthenware pots, so breaking them would be unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a metal oven, which fire can clean. Earthenware pots cannot be cleaned and must be broken, as רב says.

steps.title: A second answer: heat from inside versus heat from outside
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא can also be about a clay oven. Its fire burns inside it, which cleans it. A pot sits on the fire and is heated only from outside, which does not clean it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say the ברייתא is talking about a clay oven. This one (the oven) is heated from inside, and that one (the pot) is heated from outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to explain why firing cleans an oven while רב says pots must be broken for פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer split metal from clay. This answer keeps both items clay and splits them by where the fire is. Fire burning inside a vessel draws out what it soaked up. Heat that only reaches the outside does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Or if you want, say: it introduces a second, alternative answer

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not cancel the metal-oven answer. The גמרא offers two separate ways to answer the same question.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
it is about a clay oven;
this one is heated from the inside,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the oven, where the fire burns inside it.

phrases.english: and that one is heated from the outside.
phrases.notes: "That one" is the pot, which sits on top of the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, alternative answer to רבינא's question, alongside the metal-oven answer from Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (where the heat is applied)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Firing cleans an oven, so firing should clean clay pots too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only fire burning inside a vessel cleans it. A pot heated from outside stays forbidden, even though both are clay.

steps.title: Why not heat the pots from inside?
steps.stepSummary: If inside heat cleans clay, people could simply light a fire inside their pots and keep them.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let us heat the pots from inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the new answer: if inside heat works, why must anyone break their pots?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 17 made cleaning depend on where the fire is. If that is the only problem, there is an easy fix: put the fire inside the pot. Then רב's rule to break pots seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: So let us do: a suggestion that pushes back

phrases.english: So let us do the heating from inside!
phrases.notes: This means heating the pots from inside, the same way an oven is heated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inside/outside answer of Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that pots must be broken for פסח, now that Step 17 says inside heat cleans clay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If inside heat cleans clay, pots could be cleaned that way, so breaking them should not be needed.

steps.title: People worry the pots will crack
steps.stepSummary: Owners protect their pots because strong heat would crack them, so they will not heat them enough to clean them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is careful with them, because they break.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why inside heating is not a real option for pots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside heating would work in theory. The problem is human: a clay pot cracks under strong heat, so the owner will hold back. Since we cannot trust the pot to be heated enough, the only safe rule is to break it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is careful with, protects (worries about losing)

steps.whyThisMatters: According to this second answer, רב's rule to break pots is not because clay can never be cleaned. It is because people cannot be relied on to heat their own pots enough.

phrases.english: He is careful with them, since they break.
phrases.notes: "He" is the pot's owner. He won't heat them strongly enough, so they don't really get cleaned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical concern (we fear the owner will not heat the pots enough)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pots could be heated from inside and cleaned.
steps.terutzMaskana: Owners would hold back so the pots don't crack, so pots must be broken.

steps.title: A clay baking tile stays forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Because outside heating does not clean, a clay baking tile (כוביא), which is heated from outside, is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, this baking tile: it is heated from outside, and it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a practical rule from the inside/outside answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כוביא is a clay tile set on the fire for baking, so the fire touches it only from outside. By the rule of Step 17, outside heat does not draw out what it soaked up. So it cannot be cleaned that way and stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A clay baking tile set on the fire

steps.whatToRemember: Fire burning inside a clay vessel cleans it, like an oven. Heat from outside does not, like a pot or a כוביא. Pots must be broken because owners won't heat them hard enough from inside.

phrases.english: Therefore, this baking tile –
its heating is from outside, and it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the inside/outside rule to a practical case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A clay baking tile heated from outside cannot be cleaned by that heat and stays forbidden.
